From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Thomas Berg <t.berg@nordbank.eu>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 08:15:00 +0200
Subject: Deployment & data residency — hosted vs dedicated vs private (post-call)

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on requirements: 

TL;DR: You indicated NordBank needs strict EU data residency for customer data, potential cross-region read-only analytics in the US for aggregated metrics, and are evaluating Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem for production.

Key items from the call:
- Residency: primary requirement is that customer PII and transaction logs remain in EU-controlled infrastructure.
- Hosting options: you asked whether Redwood Hosted API can guarantee EU-only storage/processing, and when EU regions are generally available.
- Dedicated: interest in reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput and isolation — asked about network isolation and contractual SLAs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): mentioned as a potential requirement if third-party access to metadata is unacceptable.
- Next steps we agreed: 1) I’ll send our short deployment-options doc and SOC2 answers; 2) schedule a technical call with Vivek (solutions engineering) to validate network/architecture constraints; 3) procurement will need ballpark pricing and contract flow.

Attached: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (short comparison), soc2-answers.xlsx (SOC2 checklist answers), nordbank-mrap.xlsx (initial MRA/processing notes).

Notes on residency and routing (high-level):
- Hosted API: Redwood runs hosted inference in regionally isolated clusters. We currently operate an EU region (eu-west-1) that processes and stores tokens and request logs within EU-resident infrastructure. For customers who require EU residency, we can set routing policies to constrain traffic to EU regions — this is the simplest path if your regulatory needs are met by regional controls and contractual commitments.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Reserved GPU pools can be provisioned in the EU region and provide stronger tenancy isolation, with optional private networking (VPC peering) and stricter lifecycle controls for logs. This is commonly selected when teams need predictable throughput and stronger isolation than multi-tenant hosted.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): For the strictest residency and control (air-gapped or customer-managed infrastructure), Redwood Private deploys in your VPC or on-prem. This supports on-prem KMS/HSM, customer-controlled audit logs, and removes cross-tenant data surface area.

Question for you (to prep for the SE call):
1) Do you require absolute prohibition on any cross-region replication of request-level logs, or is aggregated, anonymized metrics in the US acceptable?
2) Are there any procurement or legal constraints (e.g., mandatory on-prem deployment) that would make Hosted/Dedicated infeasible?

Proposed next steps:
- Can we schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Vivek this week or next? He’ll walk the architecture options and validate network/firewall needs.
- I’ll include a preliminary ballpark pricing range for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private in the follow-up.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your preferred times.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying points from our side before the SE call: 

1) Residency: We need all customer-identifiable data (transaction logs, prompts/outputs tied to customer IDs) to remain in the EU. Aggregated telemetry that cannot be tied back to customers may be sent outside EU (to our analytics partner in the US) but only if it is anonymized and approved by our legal team.

2) Hosted: If Hosted guarantees EU-only processing and storage (contractually), that would be simplest. We need to understand what "EU-only" means in practice (where backups live, any support tooling that calls home, etc.).

3) Private: If Hosted/Dedicated still has any EU->US replication for backups or telemetry, we will likely need Private deployment. Curious on the effort/timeline/cost delta for Private compared to Dedicated.

4) SE call: available Wed 15 Jul 09:00-11:00 CET or Thu 16 Jul 14:00-16:00 CET. Please also include a short runbook that shows where logs and backups are stored.

Also copying procurement (procurement@nordbank.eu) on commercial timing — they’ll want ballpark numbers and procurement steps.

Thanks — Elise

Hi Elise — great questions, answered inline below. I’ve attached the short runbook Vivek will walk through on the call.

1) "EU-only" definition: For Hosted we offer a contractual data residency addendum that specifies processing, short-term caches, and persistent logs for that tenant are stored and processed in the selected region (eu-west-1). Backups are retained in-region by default; we can add contractual language to prohibit replication outside EU. Support tooling that needs access to logs can be scoped to run from EU-only consoles or via Red-team access controls — we’ll show exactly how this is enforced on the SE call.

2) Cross-region analytics: Aggregated, anonymized telemetry sent to a US analytics partner is feasible — we can provide an allowlist/denylist and a transformation step (hashing/anonymization) before any export. If your legal team requires no export at all, the Private option removes that vector.

3) Dedicated vs Private effort & timeline (ballpark):
- Dedicated (EU-hosted reserved capacity): ~2-4 weeks provisioning + network setup and contract signature. Lower engineering overhead; Redwood manages runtime but you get tenancy isolation and VPC peering options.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): ~6-12 weeks depending on your infra readiness and KMS integration. Requires collaboration with your infra team for networking and possibly on-prem provisioning. Higher one-time setup cost; lower control plane exposure.

4) Cost direction (very rough):
- Hosted (EU tenancy): lowest setup effort, pay-as-you-go usage pricing.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): mid-to-high monthly commit, predictable throughput; OPEX style pricing.
- Private: highest setup cost (one-time) plus license/maintenance; good for strict compliance needs.

5) Attachments: runbook (redwood-deployment-options.pdf) describes where logs/backups live, and an export workflow. I’ve also attached the SOC2 answers we discussed.

Proposed schedule: Wed 15 Jul 09:30 CET for the SE deep-dive (I booked Vivek and 60 minutes). If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a pre-read (short architecture diagram + runbook).

If procurement wants a one-pager pricing matrix before the call, I can include a ballpark table in the invite.

—
